name: Dagon
overview: Dagon was a prominent idol worshiped by the Philistines, whose temple served as a place of worship and sacrifice, as seen when the Philistines gathered to offer a great sacrifice to him after capturing Samson (Judges 16:23). The ark of God was placed in the house of Dagon in Ashdod, but the idol repeatedly fell before the ark, losing its head and hands, demonstrating the superiority of the God of Israel over this false god (1 Samuel 5:1-5). As a result, even the priests and worshippers of Dagon avoided treading on the temple's threshold, acknowledging the power of the LORD over their idol.
